not_covered.text: An al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula attack in Shabwah Governorate kills two soldiers.
The European Parliament awards its 2026 Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials for their work in global justice and upholding international law.
At least six people are killed and 25 others are injured when a bus collides with a tree in Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur district, Chhattisgarh, India.

not_covered.topic: Canada–Turkey relations, Free trade agreements of Canada, Free trade agreements of Turkey
not_covered.text: Canada and Turkey open negotiations for a free trade agreement during Canadian prime minister Mark Carney's visit to Ankara.
Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh announces her candidacy to Secretary-General of the United Nations.
A Guatemalan court sentences seven former police officers to prison terms of up to 60 years for offenses related to the 2024 torture and killing of a gay couple at a police station.
Ecuadorian opposition leader and former presidential candidate Luisa González is arrested over allegations on money laundering in campaign financing.

The Finnish Government grants Posiva an operating license for the Onkalo spent nuclear fuel repository in Eurajoki, making it the world's first licensed deep geological disposal facility for spent nuclear fuel.
In women's association football, FIFA announces that the United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women's Club World Cup in 2028.

The Athletics Integrity Unit bans Ethiopian marathon runner Ruti Aga for six years after she tested positive for methylprednisolone and submitted false information and a forged prescription during an investigation.
